sites.name: Phong Nha Cave
sites.event: A UNESCO World Natural Heritage site, dubbed the 'First Cave Wonder' with the longest underground river system.

sites.name: Vung Chua - Yen Island
sites.event: The final resting place of General Vo Nguyen Giap - the eldest brother of the People's Army of Vietnam.

sites.name: Son Doong Cave
sites.event: The world's largest natural cave, possessing a pristine primeval forest ecosystem and its own unique climate right inside the cave.

sites.name: Quang Binh Gate
sites.event: One of the important checkpoints of the Luy Thay (Dao Duy Tu Wall) system, built in 1639 during the Nguyen Lords era.

sites.name: Paradise Cave
sites.event: Dubbed the 'Underground Palace', it is the longest dry cave in Asia with a magnificent system of stalactites and stalagmites.

sites.name: Tam Co Cave
sites.event: A historical relic on Route 20 Quyet Thang, marking the tragic sacrifice of 8 youth volunteers buried by US bombs in 1972.

sites.name: Da Nhay Beach
sites.event: A beautiful beach with a diverse complex of rocks of all shapes and sizes bobbing with the waves, which was once the filming location for the movie 'The Immortal'.

sites.name: Mother Suot Monument
sites.event: A symbol of patriotism, commemorating Mother Nguyen Thi Suot who rowed boats to transport soldiers across the Nhat Le River under a rain of bombs and bullets.

place.commune: Bao Ninh Ward (The monument is located on the riverbank of the former Hai Dinh Ward)

sites.name: Mooc Spring
sites.event: A famous eco-tourism destination with cool, turquoise water rising from the foot of the limestone mountain.

sites.name: Tam Toa Church Bell Tower Relic
sites.event: A testament to war crimes, the remaining ruins of the Catholic church destroyed by US bombs in 1965.

sites.name: Hoang Phuc Pagoda
sites.event: One of the oldest pagodas in Central Vietnam (dating back to 1314), where King-Monk Tran Nhan Tong once visited and preached.

sites.name: General Vo Nguyen Giap Memorial House
sites.event: The simple 3-compartment wooden house where General Vo Nguyen Giap was born and raised.
